headline: Pricing gains and cost discipline drive a sharp profit jump
summary_short: Operating revenues rose 10.4% y/y to $1.57 billion and income from operations jumped 30% to $71.4 million, lifting diluted EPS to $0.28 from $0.20 a year ago.
summary_long: Schneider's earnings grew across all three segments: Truckload operating income rose 28% on improved Network pricing and productivity, Logistics rose 53% on higher revenue per order and cost actions, and Intermodal rose 14% on fuel-surcharge recovery and volume. Net income increased 38% to $49.7 million and adjusted diluted EPS rose 38% to $0.29. Cash grew to $292.7 million on six-month operating cash flow of $264.3 million against $122.0 million of investing and $51.1 million of financing outflows. The company raised full-year 2026 adjusted diluted EPS guidance to $0.90-$1.10 (from $0.70-$1.00) and lowered net capex guidance to $350-$400 million (from $400-$450 million), reflecting lower trailing-equipment spend.

drivers.explanation: Management credits disciplined revenue management, cost reduction, and productivity actions, plus non-compliant capacity exiting the market, for stronger operating leverage.

Truckload revenue rose on improved Network pricing/productivity (Dedicated volume lower); Logistics rose 11% on higher revenue per order; Intermodal fell 1% on shorter length of haul; fuel surcharge revenue also rose.

Truckload operating income rose 28% on Network pricing/productivity, fuel-surcharge recovery, and equipment-sale gains; Intermodal rose 14% on fuel recovery and volume; Logistics rose 53% on revenue-per-order and cost actions.
EPS growth tracks the 38% net income increase against an essentially flat diluted share count (176.0M vs 175.7M shares).
Six-month operating cash flow of $264.3M exceeded $122.0M of investing outflows and $51.1M of financing outflows, per the cash-flow statement.
